title: Automated Real Estate Wholesaling System -- Research Packet
summary: Real estate wholesaling is a viable revenue stream that can be substantially automated with AI. California is legal but faces pending legislation (AB 1850) that may require a license. Average assignment fees are $10k-$25k per deal. Zillow API is dead; alternatives exist at $0.01-$0.25/record.

1_zillow_data_access.zillow_api_status: DEPRECATED. Zillow sunset its original public API (Zillow Data API) in April 2021. All accounts were migrated to Bridge Interactive Data API. Zillow no longer offers a free public API for bulk listing data.

bridge_interactive.description: Zillow Group's replacement. Provides MLS listing data via RESO Web API standard.
bridge_interactive.access: Requires MLS partnership or approved business use case. Not open to individual wholesalers.

zillow_scraping.feasibility: Technically possible via tools like Apify ($49+/mo) or ScrapingBee. Zillow pages are public.
zillow_scraping.legal_risk: HIGH. Zillow's Terms of Service prohibit scraping. They have sent cease-and-desist letters. Not recommended as a primary data source for a business system.
zillow_scraping.note: Scraping for personal lead research is common but building a commercial system on it is legally risky.

2_california_legality.current_status: LEGAL with conditions. Wholesaling via contract assignment is legal in California as of March 2026. No real estate license is required IF you only assign your contractual rights and do not market properties you do not own.
key_statutes: CA Business & Professions Code Section 10016 -- defines real estate broker
CA Business & Professions Code Section 10130 -- licensure requirements
CA Business & Professions Code Section 10131 -- broker activities

pending_legislation.status: Introduced, may be heard in committee March 14, 2026. NOT YET LAW.
pending_legislation.impact: Would REQUIRE a real estate license to wholesale. Would expand the definition of 'broker' to include anyone entering a purchase contract with intent to assign for profit.
pending_legislation.disclosure_requirements: Would require written disclosure to seller that wholesaler does not intend to take title. All ads must disclose the person does not hold legal title.
pending_legislation.risk_assessment: MEDIUM-HIGH. If passed, this fundamentally changes the wholesaling landscape in CA. Monitor closely.

compliance_requirements_current: Always disclose your role as assignor to the seller
Use explicit assignment clauses in purchase agreements
Seller must agree in writing that the contract can be assigned
Do NOT market the property itself -- market your contractual interest
Do NOT represent yourself as the owner or an agent
Keep all earnest money deposits in proper escrow

assignment_fee.description: You sign a purchase agreement with seller (A-B contract), then assign your position to end buyer (C) for a fee. One closing. Simplest method.
assignment_fee.pros: Low cost, fast, no need to close yourself
assignment_fee.cons: Fee is visible to all parties. Some sellers/title companies refuse assignments.

double_close.description: Two separate transactions: you buy from seller (A-B), then immediately sell to end buyer (B-C). Two closings, same day or within days.
double_close.pros: Fee is hidden. Works when assignments are blocked. More professional appearance.
double_close.cons: Higher closing costs (two sets of title fees). Need transactional funding ($500-2000 for short-term lending).
double_close.typical_fee: Same range, but absorbed into the price spread

finder_fee.description: You simply refer a deal to an investor for a flat fee. No contract assignment.
finder_fee.cons: Smallest fees ($500-$2,000). May still constitute unlicensed brokerage in CA.
finder_fee.warning: In California, accepting a finder's fee for real estate referrals without a license is legally gray. The DRE has taken the position this requires a license.

distressed_seller_signals.data_source: USPS vacancy data, PropStream, utility records

deal_flow: 1. DATA PULL: Pull property lists filtered by distress signals (PropStream/ATTOM API)
2. SKIP TRACE: Append owner phone/email via skip tracing service
3. OUTREACH: Multi-channel automated contact (SMS, ringless voicemail, direct mail, cold call)
4. QUALIFY: Assess motivation, timeline, property condition, price expectations
5. OFFER: Calculate MAO (Maximum Allowable Offer) = ARV x 0.70 - Repairs - Your Fee
6. CONTRACT: Get property under purchase agreement with assignment clause
7. MARKET TO BUYERS: Blast deal to investor buyer list with property details and photos
8. ASSIGN: Execute assignment agreement with end buyer, collect assignment fee
9. CLOSE: Title company handles closing, you get paid at settlement
building_buyer_list: Attend local REIA (Real Estate Investors Association) meetings
Pull recent cash buyer transactions from county records (ATTOM API)
Facebook groups: local real estate investor groups
Build email list via landing page on your site
Network with hard money lenders (they know active buyers)
PropStream can filter for recent cash buyers in your target market

fully_automatable: CRM lead tracking and follow-up reminders
Buyer list blast emails when new deals are found
partially_automatable: Seller qualification calls (AI voice agents emerging, but human touch still converts better)
Property condition assessment (can use satellite/street view imagery + AI, but walkthroughs matter)
Offer negotiation (AI can draft, human should handle)

assignment_fee_ranges.source: Real Estate Bees 2026 survey, PropPipeline 2025 report

conversion_funnel.marketing_to_lead: 0.5-2% response rate on outreach (direct mail, SMS, cold call)

solo_operator_realistic_volume.note: AI automation can meaningfully reduce the gap between intermediate and advanced by automating list building, skip tracing, and initial outreach. The human bottleneck is seller negotiations and contract execution.

6_everlight_integration_opportunities.broker_os_synergy: Wholesaling deal flow can feed into Broker OS as a deal type. Investor buyer matching is essentially B2B matchmaking -- same architecture.
6_everlight_integration_opportunities.django_dashboard: Deal pipeline tracking, KPI dashboards, seller/buyer CRM can all live in the existing Django hive_dashboard.
6_everlight_integration_opportunities.supabase_backend: Lead data, deal status, buyer lists, assignment contracts can all be stored in Supabase tables.
6_everlight_integration_opportunities.ai_automation_layer: Claude/AI agents can handle: list scoring, offer calculation (MAO formula), outreach copy generation, deal analysis summaries for buyers.
6_everlight_integration_opportunities.revenue_stream_fit: At $15k+ per deal, even 1 deal/month would be the highest-margin revenue stream in the Everlight portfolio.
recommended_mvp: 1. Sign up for PropStream ($99/mo) -- immediate access to distressed property lists in your target CA market
2. Use ATTOM API free trial to prototype automated data pulls
3. Build a simple lead pipeline in Supabase: leads -> contacted -> qualified -> under_contract -> assigned -> closed
5. Set up SMS outreach via BatchDialer or Launch Control
6. Build a buyer list landing page on everlightventures.io
7. First deal target: 60-90 days from start

risk_notes: CRITICAL: Monitor CA AB 1850. If passed, wholesaling in CA will require a real estate license. This could add 135+ hours of coursework and exam requirements.
TCPA compliance for SMS/calls is non-negotiable. Violations are $500-$1,500 per message. Register for 10DLC, scrub DNC lists.
Zillow scraping for commercial use carries legal risk. Use legitimate APIs.
Assignment fee visibility can cause deal friction. Consider double-close capability.
Title companies vary in willingness to handle assignments. Build relationships with investor-friendly title companies early.
